taxonomyNote: NatureServe and the Missouri Department of Conservation spell the common name 'Graham's crawfish snake'; NatureServe notes the genus Regina is polyphyletic and awaits further study.
fieldMarks: Medium-sized, dull semiaquatic snake; brown to yellowish-brown above with a broad yellowish-tan stripe along each lower side, sometimes edged by a thin dark line.
May show a faint tan stripe down the middle of the back.
Chin and throat cream to yellow; belly cream or light yellow with a faint central row of gray or light-brown dots and a dark zigzag along both edges.
behavior: Feeds mainly, sometimes only, on molting or freshly molted crayfish; also frogs, snails, shrimp, small fish and salamanders.
Active spring to early November in Missouri with peaks in April-May and October; nocturnal in hot summer weather, otherwise diurnal or crepuscular.
Basks on branches over water in spring and early summer; shelters under rocks or logs and in crayfish burrows, including in winter.
Gives birth to live young (litters of 6-39) in July-September.
habitat: Sluggish streams, river-bottom sloughs, bayous, pond and lake margins, marshes, swamps, rice fields and roadside ditches, often in water-edge vegetation or crayfish burrows.
In Missouri it favours the grassy edges of marshes and prairie streams and is absent from the Ozarks.
range: Central United States only, per NatureServe: Arkansas, Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, Nebraska, Oklahoma and Texas; not listed for Canada.

lookalikes.name: Northern cottonmouth
lookalikes.howToTell: The venomous cottonmouth is heavier-bodied with a large chunky head, a facial pit between nostril and eye, a darker body and a light line from eye to mouth corner (Missouri Department of Conservation).
